products.superPrompt:
You are a habit-tracker designer who writes in a direct, Gen Z-friendly voice. Your goal: write the complete content for a dated printable tracker called "Lock-In: The Final 12 Weeks of 2026".

BUYER AND JOB
The buyer is 18-30 and doing a late-year "lock-in" they saw on TikTok. There are no official rules, so they want structure: three non-negotiables, a daily check grid, a weekly reflection, and a proof log where they write real numbers (pages read, workouts done, dollars saved) to show progress.

DATES (use exactly; every week runs Monday-Sunday, 2026)
Week 1 Oct 5-11, Week 2 Oct 12-18, Week 3 Oct 19-25, Week 4 Oct 26-Nov 1, Week 5 Nov 2-8, Week 6 Nov 9-15, Week 7 Nov 16-22, Week 8 Nov 23-29, Week 9 Nov 30-Dec 6, Week 10 Dec 7-13, Week 11 Dec 14-20, Week 12 Dec 21-27. Close-out: Dec 28-31.

DELIVERABLE: 21 pages, US Letter 8.5x11 in and A4
1 Cover: "LOCK-IN" / "The Final 12 Weeks of 2026" / "Oct 5 - Dec 27" / "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
2 My Lock-In Rules: three non-negotiables, each with the habit, the minimum version for a bad day, how I'll measure it, and when and where. Two printed rules: "One planned rest day a week is part of the plan." "Missed a day? Restart the next day."
3 Joining Late?: start at the current week, cross out the weeks already gone, start the proof log today.
4 Starting Numbers: three metrics, each with unit and starting value; "Why this matters to me" line.
5 12-Week Overview: 12 rows (week number + dates) x 7 day columns, one box per day.
6-17 Weekly pages, one per week: header "WEEK [n] | [dates]"; check grid of 3 rows (non-negotiables) plus a rest-day row x 7 columns (Mon-Sun); "One line a day" (7 short lines); "This week's numbers" (3 metrics); Reflection: what worked, what got in the way, one adjustment for next week; "Energy this week" 1-5 circles. Week 6 adds a "Halfway check" box.
18-19 Proof Log: table of Weeks 1-12 x Metrics 1-3 with a running-total column, then a bar grid (12 columns x 20 rows) to shade by hand.
20 Final Review (Dec 27): totals, proudest moment, what I learned, keep / drop for 2027.
21 Close-Out Dec 28-31: four-day mini grid and "Carry it into 2027" (three habits I'm keeping, one I'm adding), with the line "Continue in [YOUR 2027 PLANNER NAME]".

DESIGN
Bold, grid-based, plenty of white space. Headings Anton, all caps; body Inter. Palette "Locked Charcoal": Charcoal #1C1C1E, Off-White #F5F5F0, Signal Lime #C6F432 (accents only), Steel Gray #8A8F98, Warm Sand #E8DCC8. Add an ink-saver note: outlines instead of solid fills. Give rows, columns and labels for every grid.

CONTENT RULES
Original wording; short sentences; about a 6th-grade reading level; confident and encouraging, never shaming. Metrics belong to the buyer; use only neutral examples (pages read, sessions completed, dollars set aside, minutes practiced).

WHY THIS IS BETTER
Generic undated trackers don't know about the 2026 lock-in. This one is dated to it, adds a proof log for numbers, and builds in a minimum version and a rest day, which answers the "grind culture" burnout criticism.

CONSTRAINTS
No health, fitness, weight, money or success promises. No brand, app, creator or influencer names. Do not use "Winter Arc" or "12 Week Year" as titles. Generic slang only.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Page by page: "=== PAGE [n]: [title] ===", "Layout:" (one line), then exact text, fill-in lines "______", and grids written as "Grid: [rows] x [columns]; row labels ...; column labels ...". Write the weekly page once as a template, then list the 12 header lines. End with:
SELF-CHECK (fix any "no"): 21 pages; the 12 weeks match the date list exactly; every weekly page has 3 non-negotiable rows plus a rest row; no outcome promises; no brand or person names; wording original.

assembly: Before naming the listing, search USPTO's free Trademark Search for "LOCK IN", "LOCK-IN" and "GREAT LOCK-IN". If a live mark covers paper goods or downloadable printables, retitle around "Final 12 Weeks".
Paste the super prompt into Claude or ChatGPT and check that the 12 week dates match exactly (Monday Oct 5 to Sunday Dec 27, 2026).

In Canva, create a US Letter design (8.5 x 11 in) using Anton and Inter and the Locked Charcoal palette. Build the weekly page with Elements > Table (4 rows x 8 columns: label column plus Mon-Sun), duplicate it 12 times and edit the headers.
Build the remaining pages (rules, joining late, starting numbers, overview, proof log, final review, close-out) and add the cover from the image prompt or Canva text.
Export PDF Print (300 DPI). For A4, use Resize (paid plan) or copy the pages into an A4 design and export again. Save an ink-saver version with outlines instead of fills if you have time.
List on Etsy (Letter and A4 PDFs) and on Gumroad at the same price.
Prepare an undated "any 12 weeks" copy (remove the dates) so you can switch to the free lead-magnet pivot in minutes.
Make 5 pins (1000x1500) and film 3 vertical videos (1080x1920) using printed pages.

Write the Etsy listing for my printable "Lock-In: The Final 12 Weeks of 2026" tracker: dated Monday Oct 5 to Sunday Dec 27, 2026, with a rules page for 3 non-negotiables, a "joining late" page, starting numbers, a 12-week overview, 12 weekly check-grid pages, a proof log for recording your own numbers, a final review and a Dec 28-31 close-out page. 21 pages; US Letter and A4 PDFs. Produce:
1. TITLE under 140 characters starting with the buyer's search phrase (for example "Lock In Tracker 2026" or "Last 12 Weeks of 2026 Tracker"), then key features. Give 3 options and mark your pick.
2. 13 TAGS, each 20 characters or fewer (show each count), no repeats, covering lock in tracker, 12 week tracker, habit tracker 2026, goal tracker, last 12 weeks, proof log, accountability and printable.
3. DESCRIPTION: two-line opener; "What's inside" bullets; "Files and sizes"; "How delivery works" (instant download from Etsy Purchases; nothing ships; print at home); "Joining late?" products.superPrompt:
You are a planner designer and a plain-spoken productivity writer. Your goal: write the complete content for "Lock In 2027", a 12-week Q1 sprint planner sold as a printable PDF and a hyperlinked tablet PDF, with an optional paperback interior later.

BUYER AND JOB
The buyer is an 18-35-year-old resolution skeptic who prefers short sprints and a "rebrand" to January resolutions. The planner carries the lock-in identity into the New Year: a vision page, up to three measurable goals, 12 dated weeks, proof logs and an optional low-buy tracker.

DATES (use exactly)
2027 starts on Friday, January 1. Setup week: Mon Dec 28, 2026 to Sun Jan 3, 2027. Week 1 Jan 4-10, Week 2 Jan 11-17, Week 3 Jan 18-24, Week 4 Jan 25-31, Week 5 Feb 1-7, Week 6 Feb 8-14, Week 7 Feb 15-21, Week 8 Feb 22-28, Week 9 Mar 1-7, Week 10 Mar 8-14, Week 11 Mar 15-21, Week 12 Mar 22-28. Review week: Mar 29 to Apr 4. February 2027 has 28 days.

DELIVERABLE: 44 pages
1 Cover: "LOCK IN 2027" / "12-Week Sprint Planner" / "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
2 How It Works: why one 12-week sprint, how to use setup week, how proof logs work.
3 My 2027 Rebrand: "Who I'm becoming" (three "I'm someone who..." lines), Keep / Drop / Start lists, three words for my year.
4 2027 at a Glance: 12 mini-calendars, Monday start.
5 Four Sprints Map: Q1 dated; Q2, Q3 and Q4 blank with date lines.
6 Q1 Goals: up to 3 goals, each with Why, Finish line (a number), January / February / March milestones, weekly actions, minimum version.
7 Non-Negotiables and Rules: 3 daily non-negotiables, 1 weekly one, one planned rest day.
8 Starting Numbers: metric, unit, starting value, finish line.
9-32 Weekly spreads, 2 pages per week for 12 weeks. Left: "WEEK [n] | [dates]", top 3 outcomes, check grid (3 non-negotiables x Mon-Sun), simple day blocks Mon-Sun. Right: this week's numbers, wins, misses, one adjustment, "Locked-in score" 1-10. Week 6 adds a midpoint review.
33-35 Monthly Habit Trackers: January (31 days), February (28), March (31); 8 habit rows each.
36-37 Proof Log: Weeks 1-12 x 3 metrics with running totals, then a 12-column bar grid to shade.
38-39 Low-Buy Tracker (optional): my rules (always OK / not this sprint / wait 48 hours), January-March no-spend-day calendars, "Skipped purchases" log (item, amount, date).
40 Week 13 Review (Mar 29-Apr 4): finish line vs result, what worked, keep / drop, next sprint focus.
41-44 Notes.

DESIGN
Tablet: 1620x2160 px portrait with a right-edge tab strip (Rebrand, Goals, W1-W12, Habits, Proof, Low-Buy, Review). Printable: US Letter 8.5x11 in and A4, 0.5 in margins, no tabs. Headings Montserrat ExtraBold, all caps; body Inter. Palette "Fresh Start Graphite": Graphite #22252A, Paper #FAF8F3, Electric Cobalt #2F5BEA, Mint #9ED8C3, Pale Gray #D9DCE1. Clean grids, high contrast, no florals.

CONTENT RULES
Original, direct, second-person copy at about a 7th-grade level; motivating without hype or shame. Example metrics stay neutral (pages read, sessions done, dollars set aside, hours practiced).

WHY THIS IS BETTER
Instead of a year-long planner that is easy to drop, it is one focused quarter with lock-in framing, proof logs that show progress in numbers, and the rebrand and low-buy rituals in one place. Minimum versions and a rest day keep it sustainable.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not use the phrase "12 Week Year", commercial planner or app names, creator names, or "Winter Arc" as a title. No promises about health, fitness, weight, income, savings or success. The low-buy pages are a personal log, not financial advice.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Page by page: "=== PAGE [n]: [title] ===", "Layout:" (one line), exact text, fill-in lines "______", grids as rows x columns with labels. Write the weekly spread once as a template, then list the 12 header lines. Then a HYPERLINK MAP (tab or index item -> page number). End with:
SELF-CHECK (fix any "no"): 44 pages; Week 1 starts Monday Jan 4 and Week 12 ends Sunday Mar 28; February shows 28 days; no outcome promises; no trademarked titles or brand names; wording original.
